requirements.text: Ensure that a high impact and high urgency incident is registered for this issue ... facing issue with the Main Printer (serial number: PRT-ACME-01)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_101' AND caller_id = 'USER_051' AND configuration_item = 'CI_096' AND channel = 'chat' AND status = 'new' AND category = 'hardware' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_101 after INC_100)
caller resolved from the seed: Steven Manning is USER_051 (reporter, active, ORG_005), the only Manning among four Stevens

CI resolved from the seed by serial: PRT-ACME-01 is CI_096 'Main Printer - ACME HQ' (status in_use, location LOC_001 'ACME HQ', Santa Clara, USA; owner USER_031, the acting user), so the policy allows linking it; CI_091 'Reception Printer - Globex' (PRT-GLB-001) is the near match
channel not stated; the policy's default is chat
status new is the policy's default state for a new incident (the column is status in this schema)
category hardware kept from the benchmark check; the policy makes category mandatory and a printer fault is hardware in the seed's category vocabulary
impact high and urgency high are stated; priority critical follows from the policy's Impact x Urgency matrix
the caller is in ORG_005 and the CI in ORG_001; both are what the request names, so no cell is dropped for the mismatch and the incident's org_id is not tested
the location, the Friday deadline and the client meeting have no incident column and are not tested; short_description is mandatory but free text and not tested

stage in_progress kept from the benchmark check; a freshly linked SLA is running
two SLA rows are created in this table (the seed has two active definitions for critical), so the row is selected by its natural key (incident, definition), not by id

requirements.text: Provide with an appropriate knowledge article to be used as resolution for the issue ... causing paper jams
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident_knowledge WHERE incident_kb_id = 'IKB_046' AND incident_id = 'INC_101' AND knowledge_id = 'KB_013' AND used_as = 'suggested'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (IKB_046 after IKB_045); the request asks for one article, so one link
KB_013 'Printer Jam - Tray 2' (published, external) is the seed's only article on printers or paper jams

used_as suggested kept from the benchmark check: policy section 7 links articles found by search as suggested and reserves resolution for an article that resolves the incident, which is registered as new here; 'to be used as resolution' is read as the article's purpose

disagreement: used_as: A suggested, B resolution; chose suggested because the benchmark's check is the prior and the request's phrase does not plainly contradict it: the incident is registered, not resolved, and policy 7 ties the resolution type to resolving the incident
